case.limits: The server test is a Ninth Circuit rule and has been rejected elsewhere. It also addresses display rather than the reproduction that training involves.
case.holding: Image search thumbnails were fair use, and the court adopted a server test under which a site that merely frames an image hosted elsewhere does not display it for copyright purposes.

case.why_ai_cites_it: It extends Arriba Soft to a commercial search product and supplies the argument that a system pointing at content is doing something different from a system republishing it.

reading.body:
The most important thing *Perfect 10 v. Amazon* contributes to AI copyright disputes is the argument that pointing at content is legally distinct from reproducing it, a distinction defendants invoke when arguing that model training differs from republishing protected work.

The Ninth Circuit held in 2007 that thumbnail images in search results were fair use, and adopted a server test: a service that frames or links to content hosted elsewhere does not "display" that content for copyright purposes. AI defendants cite the case to support the broader claim that a system which references or indexes material stands in a different legal position than one that copies and stores it. The extension from *Arriba Soft* to a commercial product, Amazon, matters because it signals that commercial motive alone does not defeat the transformative use argument.

The data notes two significant limits. The server test is Ninth Circuit doctrine only and has been rejected in other jurisdictions, which means its force in any given AI lawsuit depends on where that suit is filed. More fundamentally, the case addresses the display right, not the reproduction right, and training a model involves reproduction, not merely display. The 79 live cases in which this precedent circulates include claims against OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and others where reproduction is precisely what is alleged. Whether *Perfect 10*'s reasoning reaches that question is what courts are now being asked to decide.
